PLAYED THE GAME, FILED WHAT IT TAUGHT. Wired a session-scoped bridge that serves the exact state_projection text the decision model receives, then pressed buttons through it. The first thing playing taught me was that my own bridge was sampling mid-step: an 8-frame wait reported DOWN (walkable) as no-change and then UP (blocked) as a downward move. Polling until the player stops moving measured the real walk at 14 frames and the blocked press at 2 — and showed the AGENT is correct where I was wrong (cron_runner.py:720-721,5,036-5,037 use PRESS_FRAMES=5 + STEP_FORWARD=15). Filed SETTLE-1 for the residue: 15 is one frame above the measured settle, so a longer animation (ledge/stairs/door/surf) could silently invert the state_changed signal the loop reads — a candidate contributor to DIST-1's 41% direction-locking and the 8 episodes stuck in Red's House 1F. Filed PLAY-1 to keep the bridge and pin its access model: loopback only, token required, off by default, never a global tool.
